representation: binary64 values are ulong IEEE-754 bit patterns; binary32 inputs/outputs are uint encodings
rounding_target: source CUDA round-to-nearest, ties-to-even operation boundaries

translation.log2: Pinned 16-entry POWF_INVC and POWF_LOGC tables, five POWF_A coefficients, and the exact scalar operation order are transcribed into integer-bit binary64 operations.
translation.pow: Pinned unsigned-bit special-case branches, checkint classification, sign-bias selection, subnormal normalization, overflow/underflow thresholds, binary64 product, and final RN binary32 conversion are transcribed.
translation.exp2: Called through the exp-owned soft_gfk_exp2_core_bits interface; this packet contains no exp2/log API or implementation.

base_dependency.state: The base header and its declared behavior are not centrally cleared or verified. This proposal must not be consumed until central review clears the base.

constraints: No native float or double arithmetic, approximation, generic libm replacement, or duplicated log/exp API is used.
The pow-owned log2 polynomial is kept inline with its source constants and ordered operations.

The included soft binary32, soft binary64 and exp interfaces are present in the checked-in source. Keep this proposal dependency-blocked until those shared implementations and this translation are compiled and numerically verified; no production consumer may admit it yet.
verification: MetalToolchain 27.1 compiled all four helpers together with the shared binary32/binary64 headers and executed the temporary kernel on Apple M2. Each of logf, expf, powf, and atanf matched the in-tree glibc 2.39 CPU transcription in woof/core/noahmp_libm.py exactly on 4,826 rows (zero bit mismatches each). Inputs covered special values, subnormals, thresholds and adjacent encodings, plus seeded random bit patterns/pairs. This is bounded evidence, not exhaustive certification; production consumption remains blocked by the shared primitive and consumer-level contracts.
